newsitem.title: CHINA: Shanghai copper futures end up on short-covering.
newsitem.headline: Shanghai copper futures end up on short-covering.

text.p: Shanghai copper futures ended slightly up on Tuesday due to short-covering ahead of the New Year holiday, traders said.
The most active April 1997 contract ended at 20,640 yuan ($2,487) per tonne, rising 70 yuan. It opened at 20,520 yuan, hitting an intra-day low of 20,500 and a high of 20,650.
January rose 40 to 20,300, February 10 to 20,360, March 50 20,500 and May 70 to 20,650. June did not trade, while the first traded July contract ended at 20,000.
Combined volume fell sharply to 22,770 tonnes from 56,550.
Copper opened down slightly but many investors offset their positions and took a wait-and-see attitude which pushed the contracts up for most of the session, traders said.
"Short-covering was resposible for today's rises, and many long position holders also liquidated their positions with the new year approaching," one trader said.
"All later-maturing contracts found support at the 20,500-yuan level today, indicating investors were not very optimistic about the short-term trend," he added.
